sourceAnchor.label: Sedlec Ossuary
sourceAnchor.summary: A draft Source Anchor for sacred architecture built from human remains and devotional ornament.

inspiration.title: Sedlec Ossuary
inspiration.label: Sedlec Ossuary
inspiration.summary: Bone chandeliers, skull garlands, sacred ornament, anonymous dead, and devotional architecture made from remains.
inspiration.narrative: The arrangement of human remains as sacred ornament becomes hostile architecture, devotional pressure, and evidence that the dead have been made decorative.
inspiration.caption: Bone chandeliers, skull garlands, sacred ornament, anonymous dead, and devotional architecture made from remains.

card.description: A real ossuary chapel where bones become devotional ornament, geometry, and atmosphere. Human remains are arranged into chandeliers, wall patterns, and ceremonial structures, turning the dead into architecture without fully erasing their identity as bodies. Its power comes from the collision between sacred space, reverence, display, and the uncomfortable beauty of mortality made visible. It is disturbing precisely because it transforms remains into something ordered, meaningful, and almost majestic.

inspiration.logic: The arrangement of human remains as sacred ornament becomes hostile architecture, devotional pressure, and evidence that the dead have been made decorative.

components.title: The Chapel Is Hungry
components.label: The Chapel Is Hungry
components.summary: The sacred place consumes offerings, secrets, prayers, and eventually flesh.
components.tableText: Every candle leans toward the altar. The wax has pooled into shapes like tongues, and the silence waits like an open mouth.
components.mechanics: A creature that willingly offers blood here gains advantage on one Religion check before the next dawn, but suffers 1d4 necrotic damage.
components.narrative: Use this to darken any shrine, chapel, reliquary, or village church already present in the session.

components.title: Prayers Heard Underwater
components.label: Prayers Heard Underwater
components.summary: All prayers sound distant, submerged, and slightly delayed.
components.tableText: A prayer rises from nowhere, muffled as if spoken from the bottom of a flooded grave.
components.mechanics: The first Wisdom or Religion check made here has advantage if the character remains silent for one full round.
components.narrative: Use this around altars, tombs, relics, or confession scenes.

components.title: The Saint’s Face Cracks
components.label: The Saint’s Face Cracks
components.summary: A statue, portrait, or icon splits like dry skin when a lie is spoken nearby.
components.tableText: The painted saint smiles wider. Then a crack opens across its cheek like a cut.
components.mechanics: When a creature lies within 30 feet of the icon, a visible crack appears. This does not identify the liar by itself.
components.narrative: Use to pressure social scenes without solving them for the players.

components.title: The Altar Drinks First
components.label: The Altar Drinks First
components.summary: Blood, wine, holy water, and tears vanish into the altar before anyone can use them.
components.tableText: The liquid touches the stone and disappears. A swallowing sound follows from somewhere below the altar.
components.mechanics: A creature touching the altar must make a DC 14 Wisdom save. On failure, it takes 2d6 necrotic damage and cannot benefit from healing until the start of its next turn.
components.narrative: Use this to make sacred terrain hostile and memorable.

components.title: Larvae Under the Blessing
components.label: Larvae Under the Blessing
components.summary: A healing mark twitches with tiny pale shapes beneath the skin.
components.tableText: The blessing looks golden at first. Then something pale turns beneath it, as if the light has larvae.
components.mechanics: A DC 13 Medicine or Religion check reveals the sign is alive, not infected in any ordinary sense.
components.narrative: Use to make healing, blessing, or mutation feel parasitic instead of safe.

components.title: The Bone Chapel Counts the Dead
components.label: The Bone Chapel Counts the Dead
components.summary: The chapel treats bodies as sacred numbers, and every living visitor is counted as unfinished material.
components.tableText: The bones are not decorations. They are arranged like a ledger, and the empty spaces seem measured for bodies that have not died yet.
components.mechanics: When a creature is reduced below half hit points here, one nearby bone ornament turns toward it. The next Medicine or Religion check made to identify the chapel’s pattern has advantage.
components.narrative: Use this when an existing chapel, ossuary, reliquary, or crypt needs a clear devotional horror identity.

provenance.componentTitle: The Bone Chapel Counts the Dead

components.title: Dust of Polished Bone
components.label: Dust of Polished Bone
components.summary: The air smells dry, polished, and faintly sweet, like old dust scraped from inside a skull.
components.tableText: The air has no rot in it. Only dry sweetness, candle soot, and the powdery smell of bone polished by too many hands.
components.mechanics: No mechanics required. Use as the smell layer for sacred bone architecture.
components.narrative: Use this to distinguish ossuary horror from ordinary crypt rot.

components.title: The Bones Sweat Candlewax
components.label: The Bones Sweat Candlewax
components.summary: Every bone ornament feels slick with wax, even where no candle has touched it.
components.tableText: The skull is dry to the eye, but slick under your fingers. Warm wax gathers in the sockets and clings to your skin.
components.mechanics: A creature handling the ornament has disadvantage on the next Sleight of Hand check made before it cleans its fingers.
components.narrative: Use as tactile detail when players inspect reliquaries, bone altars, or ossuary walls.

components.title: The Chandelier Has One New Rib
components.label: The Chandelier Has One New Rib
components.summary: A bone chandelier contains one fresh rib with red marrow still visible at the cut.
components.tableText: Among the yellowed ribs of the chandelier, one bone is fresh enough to glisten.
components.mechanics: A DC 13 Medicine check reveals the rib was removed within the last day.
components.narrative: Use as a visual sign that the ossuary is still collecting material.

provenance.componentTitle: The Chandelier Has One New Rib

components.title: The Skulls Turn Toward Confession
components.label: The Skulls Turn Toward Confession
components.summary: The skulls in the walls turn whenever someone speaks a secret, granting the room a brief judgmental focus.
components.tableText: Every skull in the wall turns at once. Their empty sockets settle on the speaker.
components.mechanics: Once per round, when a creature reveals a secret, confesses guilt, or names the dead, one enemy that can hear it has disadvantage on its next attack before the end of its turn.
components.narrative: Use to make a social reveal affect an encounter without changing the monster stat blocks.

components.title: The Reliquary of the Unclaimed
components.label: The Reliquary of the Unclaimed
components.summary: A small reliquary of anonymous bone protects the bearer, but only while the dead remain unnamed.
components.tableText: The reliquary is made from no famous saint. No inscription. No lineage. Only a finger bone wrapped in tarnished silver.
components.mechanics: Once per long rest, the bearer can add 1d4 to a failed death saving throw or saving throw against necrotic damage. If the bone is identified by name, the reliquary loses this property.
components.narrative: Use as an outcome that rewards the party while preserving the theme of anonymous mass death.

components.title: One Bone Still Has a Name
components.label: One Bone Still Has a Name
components.summary: Among anonymous decorative bones, one fragment still bears a hidden name, breaking the ossuary’s sacred anonymity.
components.tableText: Every bone here has been made anonymous by arrangement, polish, and prayer. Every bone except one. A name is scratched inside the curve of the rib.
components.mechanics: A DC 13 Investigation or Religion check reveals the named bone does not belong in the arrangement. Returning it to its proper grave suppresses one hazard or encounter twist in this location.
components.narrative: Use as the actionable clue in a Sedlec-inspired location: the dead are decorative because their identities were erased.

provenance.componentTitle: One Bone Still Has a Name

components.title: Bone-Lit Vestibule
components.label: Bone-Lit Vestibule
components.summary: Skulls arranged around the doorway mark each visitor as counted but not yet placed.
components.tableText: The entrance is lit by candles fixed into skulls, each flame leaning toward the deeper dark.
components.mechanics: The first loud prayer or oath makes every candle gutter and reveals a hidden footprint trail in bone dust.
components.narrative: A character may turn a skull away to suppress one omen here, but the next room gains a louder warning.

readAloud.compact: The entrance is lit by candles fixed into skulls, each flame leaning toward the deeper dark.
readAloud.extended: The entrance is lit by candles fixed into skulls. Their flames do not rise straight; each one leans toward the deeper dark, as if the passage ahead is inhaling.

readAloud.compact: The entrance is lit by candles fixed into skulls, each flame leaning toward the deeper dark.

map.feature: Skulls arranged around the doorway mark each visitor as counted but not yet placed.
map.interaction: A character may turn a skull away to suppress one omen here, but the next room gains a louder warning.
map.danger: The first loud prayer or oath makes every candle gutter and reveals a hidden footprint trail in bone dust.
map.secret: One skull is newer than the rest and still has a name scratched behind the jaw.
map.reward: A loose finger bone can serve as a one-use focus for detecting undead or consecrated ground.

components.title: Litany Engine Ossuary
components.label: Litany Engine Ossuary
components.summary: The location behaves like a devotional machine built from arranged remains.
components.tableText: Every chamber seems arranged to continue a prayer that no living voice remembers.
components.narrative: Use this as the main premise when bone ornament, worship, and architecture should feel like one system.

components.title: Bone-Dust Breath
components.label: Bone-Dust Breath
components.summary: The air carries a dry mineral taste of powdered bone.
components.tableText: The room tastes dry and mineral, as if each breath scrapes through old bone dust.
components.narrative: Use as a low-pressure read-aloud layer for ossuary rooms.

components.title: Clicking Skull Seams
components.label: Clicking Skull Seams
components.summary: Tiny clicks move through the walls whenever the room goes quiet.
components.tableText: Small clicks travel through the bonework, like teeth settling after speech.
components.narrative: Use to make silence feel responsive.

components.title: Prayer-Slip Mortar
components.label: Prayer-Slip Mortar
components.summary: The mortar is packed with folded prayer slips and pale hair.
components.tableText: The mortar between the stones has been packed with hair, ash, and old prayer slips.
components.narrative: Use as an immediate visible sign that points to the source theme.

components.title: Garland Gap
components.label: Garland Gap
components.summary: One skull is missing from a perfect garland, leaving an obvious mouth-shaped gap.
components.tableText: A skull garland runs flawlessly around the room except for one mouth-shaped gap.
components.narrative: Use as an immediate visible sign that points to the source theme.

components.title: Weight-Sermon Slab
components.label: Weight-Sermon Slab
components.summary: A pressure slab releases hanging bonework when crossed carelessly.
components.tableText: A sermon text is carved into a floor slab polished by knees and footsteps.
components.mechanics: A creature that crosses the slab without moving carefully triggers a fall of bonework; it must make a Dexterity saving throw or take bludgeoning damage and be knocked Prone.
components.narrative: Telegraph with dustless edges, hanging cords, and a carved warning about kneeling.

rules.text: A creature that crosses the slab without moving carefully triggers a fall of bonework; it must make a Dexterity saving throw or take bludgeoning damage and be knocked Prone.

components.title: Reliquary Tripwire
components.label: Reliquary Tripwire
components.summary: A thread of rosary beads pulls open a reliquary of sharp fragments.
components.tableText: A strand of beads runs ankle-high between two reliquary niches.
components.mechanics: A creature that breaks the bead-line scatters sharp relic fragments in a short line; the area becomes difficult terrain until cleared.
components.narrative: This is a trap that feels devotional rather than mechanical.

rules.text: A creature that breaks the bead-line scatters sharp relic fragments in a short line; the area becomes difficult terrain until cleared.

components.title: Miscounted Skull Row
components.label: Miscounted Skull Row
components.summary: A skull row reveals that one skull has been replaced recently.
components.tableText: One skull in the row is cleaner than the others, and the dust line behind it does not match.
components.mechanics: Investigation reveals the replacement is fresh and deliberately placed.
components.narrative: Use to point toward a recent intruder, victim, or cult act.

rules.text: Investigation reveals the replacement is fresh and deliberately placed.

components.title: Bone Chandelier Map
components.label: Bone Chandelier Map
components.summary: The chandelier’s bone pattern mirrors the room layout.
components.tableText: The bone chandelier repeats the map below in miniature, including one room no door reaches.
components.mechanics: Studying the pattern reveals a hidden chamber or alternate route.
components.narrative: Strong clue for secret rooms.

rules.text: Studying the pattern reveals a hidden chamber or alternate route.

components.title: Bonework Cover Lines
components.label: Bonework Cover Lines
components.summary: Bone ornaments create brittle cover and collapsing lines of sight.
components.tableText: Skull shelves and femur screens divide the room into narrow devotional lanes.
components.mechanics: Creatures can use bonework as half cover, but missed ranged attacks or area damage may collapse it into difficult terrain.
components.narrative: Adds tactical texture to ossuary fights.

rules.text: Creatures can use bonework as half cover, but missed ranged attacks or area damage may collapse it into difficult terrain.

components.title: Reliquary Alarm Choir
components.label: Reliquary Alarm Choir
components.summary: Opening a reliquary causes the room to answer in bone clicks.
components.tableText: When the reliquary opens, every skull niche begins clicking like a dry choir.
components.mechanics: After a reliquary is disturbed, stealth becomes harder and nearby enemies are alerted unless the sound is muffled.
components.narrative: Good twist for loot-first players.

rules.text: After a reliquary is disturbed, stealth becomes harder and nearby enemies are alerted unless the sound is muffled.

components.title: Counted Among the Bones
components.label: Counted Among the Bones
components.summary: The characters can gain passage by being symbolically counted with the dead.
components.tableText: A niche opens only after the living offer a name to be counted among the chapel dead.
components.mechanics: Offering a true name opens a hidden route or vault, but that name may later be invoked by the site.
components.narrative: Use as a reward with a future narrative cost.

rules.text: Offering a true name opens a hidden route or vault, but that name may later be invoked by the site.

components.title: Reliquary Fragment Key
components.label: Reliquary Fragment Key
components.summary: A bone fragment acts as a key to sacred locks.
components.tableText: A labeled finger bone rests in a small silver tube, warm only near locked reliquaries.
components.mechanics: The fragment opens one reliquary lock or reveals one hidden chapel mechanism.
components.narrative: Keep it small, useful, and morally uncomfortable.

rules.text: The fragment opens one reliquary lock or reveals one hidden chapel mechanism.

components.title: Reliquary Threshold
components.label: Reliquary Threshold
components.summary: Bone-fragment arch
components.tableText: Bone fragments are wired into the arch like teeth around an open mouth.
components.narrative: The arch clicks when a false prayer is spoken.

readAloud.compact: Bone fragments are wired into the arch like teeth around an open mouth.
readAloud.extended: The threshold narrows beneath an arch of relic bones, each fragment tagged with a name too faded to read.

readAloud.compact: Bone fragments are wired into the arch like teeth around an open mouth.
readAloud.extended: The threshold narrows beneath an arch of relic bones, each fragment tagged with a name too faded to read.

map.interaction: The arch clicks when a false prayer is spoken.
map.secret: One fragment is fresh and not yet labeled.
map.reward: A reliquary tube can be removed and used as a key.

components.title: Bone Chandelier Nave
components.label: Bone Chandelier Nave
components.summary: Map-like bone chandelier
components.tableText: A chandelier of bones hangs over the nave, repeating the map below in miniature.
components.mechanics: Falling bonework threatens the center if supports are broken.
components.narrative: The chandelier can be studied to reveal hidden rooms.

readAloud.extended: The nave opens beneath a bone chandelier so large it seems less hung than rooted into the ceiling.

map.secret: One missing bone marks an unseen chamber.
map.reward: A saint fragment is hidden in the chandelier pattern.

readAloud.extended: The entrance is lit by candles fixed into skulls. Their flames do not rise straight; each one leans toward the deeper dark, as if the passage ahead is inhaling.

map.feature: Skulls arranged around the doorway mark each visitor as counted but not yet placed.
map.interaction: A character may turn a skull away to suppress one omen here, but the next room gains a louder warning.
map.danger: The first loud prayer or oath makes every candle gutter and reveals a hidden footprint trail in bone dust.
map.secret: One skull is newer than the rest and still has a name scratched behind the jaw.
map.reward: A loose finger bone can serve as a one-use focus for detecting undead or consecrated ground.

locationRegions.title: Reliquary Threshold
locationRegions.label: Reliquary Threshold
locationRegions.tableText: Bone fragments are wired into the arch like teeth around an open mouth.
locationRegions.narrative: The arch clicks when a false prayer is spoken.

readAloud.compact: Bone fragments are wired into the arch like teeth around an open mouth.
readAloud.extended: The threshold narrows beneath an arch of relic bones, each fragment tagged with a name too faded to read.

map.interaction: The arch clicks when a false prayer is spoken.
map.secret: One fragment is fresh and not yet labeled.
map.reward: A reliquary tube can be removed and used as a key.

locationRegions.title: Bone Chandelier Nave
locationRegions.label: Bone Chandelier Nave
locationRegions.tableText: A chandelier of bones hangs over the nave, repeating the map below in miniature.
locationRegions.mechanics: Falling bonework threatens the center if supports are broken.
locationRegions.narrative: The chandelier can be studied to reveal hidden rooms.

readAloud.extended: The nave opens beneath a bone chandelier so large it seems less hung than rooted into the ceiling.
